o.text: Ultimately from Proto-Turkic *yapurgak (“leaf”). Developed through metathesis, compare Turkish yaprak. However, this phonological process has not occurred for all words in all dialects (see below). Cognate with Tatar яфрак (yafraq), etc.
Borrowed from Russian аква́риум (akvárium), from Latin aquarium.

From Proto-Turkic *emgek
Cognates
Cognate with Turkish emek (“labour, toil”), Turkmen emgenmek (“to work hard, to suffer”), Kazakh еңбек (eŋbek, “labour”), Uyghur ئەمگەك (emgek, “labour, toil”), Bashkir имгәк (emgäk, “labour, burden”), Tatar имгәк (imgäk, “burden, cripple”), Yakut эмэх (emeq, “rotten”), Chuvash амак (amak, “illness”). According to Starostin, not cognate with Turkish emeklemek (“to crawl”)
Borrowed from Persian پستهای (peste-'i). By surface analysis, püstə + -i.
